Successful data collection depends on well-managed fieldwork: trained field
teams, good relationships with the communities where research happens, clear
performance expectations, and systems that track every survey and respondent.
The guides in this section cover the operational side of running field data
collection.

## What You Will Find Here

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Preparing Field Teams

- [Field Staff Training](field-staff-training.qmd) - Planning and delivering
  enumerator training and survey manuals, emphasizing safety, ethics, data
  quality, and retraining
- [Community Entry and Local Leader
  Engagement](community-entry-local-leaders.qmd) - Initiating and managing
  relationships with communities and local leaders, from entry meeting to
  community exit
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Managing Field Operations

- [Managing Surveyor Performance](managing-surveyor-performance.qmd) - Planning
  productivity targets, monitoring schedules, sample assignments, and team
  motivation
- [Paper Survey Data Entry](paper-survey-data-entry.qmd) - Managing the full
  data entry process for paper surveys, including double entry, reconciliation,
  and auditing
:::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Survey and Respondent Tracking

- [About Survey and Respondent Tracking](tracking/index.qmd) - Overview of
  tracking systems for fieldwork progress and respondent follow-up
- [Why Tracking Matters](tracking/why-tracking.qmd) - How tracking systems
  prevent sample loss, minimize attrition, and ensure representative data
:::

## Getting Started

**Planning fieldwork?** Start with [Field Staff
Training](field-staff-training.qmd) and [Community
Entry](community-entry-local-leaders.qmd) before teams deploy, then set up
[tracking systems](tracking/index.qmd) before the first interview.
